text.p: Albanian Interior Minister Belul Celo tendered his resignation to President Sali Berisha on Thursday, a day after Berisha and the Socialist-led interim government argued over control of the key post.
State television quoted a statement by Berisha's office as saying that Celo had quit "for personal reasons."
Berisha had asked Socialist Prime Minister Bashkim Fino on Wednesday to propose a new minister, saying Celo had left the country and no one was in charge of the security forces.
Fino denied Celo had left his post. Amid the confusion, armed groups confronted each other in central Tirana in the early hours of Wednesday.
The Interior Ministry is responsible for the police, armed forces and secret police under a state of emergency in force since March to quell country-wide violence.
Under an accord brokered in March to set up the interim government and hold early elections, the job of interior minister belongs to Berisha's Democratic Party.
The Socialists are headed for a sweeping victory in the election and Berisha has said he will leave office once a new leftist government is in place.
